liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (4 reviews): The transition into Fire is described as spectacular and mysterious; The transition to Fire is a personal favorite and gets the reviewer every time [12][16][17][20]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser struggled a bit during the first set [18]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Bobby's slide and solo lead into a tearing performance [18]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor flows into an epic Saint of Circumstance and Deal [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-11-30.110936.mtx.chappell.sb31.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 197 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1980-11-30.128440.naks.mason.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 189 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd80-11-30.sbd-aud.sacks.2416.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 182 min; rated 4.43/5 by 58 [4]. Said about its sound: The recording is intelligently edited, well-blended, and smooth; The SBD recording sounds amazing for its era; The performance is clean and Jerry is smoking from the start [11][13][15]
- **gd1980-11-30.part.127319.aud.oade.stankiewicz.wise.minches.flac24**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 159 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- The band seemed to make magic happen at the Fox venue [16]
- There is dissent among fans regarding the quality of Scarlet Fire [22]
- Tapers were busted at the start of Ramble On Rose [2]
- Security was a nuisance, causing mic stand issues and chatter [5]
- The first set sounds like a night off compared to the second [17]
- Playin' In The Band sounds like Warren Haynes twenty years early [19]
- The 10-10-80 show is recommended for a better Scarlet Fire [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-11-30.110936.mtx.chappell.sb31.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix (SBD/AUD mix) Ratio ~ Phi [1]. Also: Taped by Dr. Bob Wagner using Nakamichi 700s with Bass EQ; Transferred and mastered by Chris Chappell using Apogee Ensemble and Peak Pro [1]
- **gd1980-11-30.128440.naks.mason.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones [3]
- **gd80-11-30.sbd-aud.sacks.2416.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [4]
- **gd1980-11-30.part.127319.aud.oade.stankiewicz.wise.minches.flac24**: taped by Jim Oade; Richie Stankiewicz; Jim Wise; transferred by David Minches; source: Set 1 - Master Audience Cassette: 2 Teac ME-120s> Sony D-5 location SBD; Set 2 - Master Audience Cassette: 2 Beyer M160s> Sony D-5 location SBD [5]. Also: Jim Oade used a JVC KD2 recorder and Teac ME-120s [5]
